ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior managers against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and China's domestic sanctions list (Ministry of Foreign Affairs). Enhanced due diligence required for any politically exposed persons (PEPs) including domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least quarterly), and upon any trigger event. Results must be documented and retained for at least 5 years. For virtual concert and digital ticketing operations, additional screening against FATF recommendations and the Wolfsberg Group standards is recommended. Any positive hit requires immediate escalation to the AML Compliance Officer and filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center (CAMLMAC) within 24 hours. The protocol must also include negative news screening and adverse media checks using reputable commercial databases (e.g., Dow Jones, Refinitiv, or World-Check).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Registration and Name Clearance Portal (via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Chinese characters, following the four-tier structure: [Administrative Division] + [Distinctive Trade Name] + [Industry/Operation Description] + [Legal Form]. For foreign investors, the trade name may be a phonetic transliteration of the foreign name into Chinese characters (e.g., using pinyin or a chosen Chinese name). The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names. English names are optional but must be registered separately and cannot be used as the primary legal name. The transliteration must comply with the 'Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration' (SAMR Order No. 34, 2021).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration with the SAMR within 15 working days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a written statement of reasons, the original rejection notice, and any supporting evidence demonstrating compliance with naming regulations. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court within 6 months. For expedited handling, the applicant may also request a pre-approval consultation with the local SAMR office. The appeal process typically takes 10-15 working days for reconsideration and 3-6 months for litigation. It is advisable to submit a revised name application simultaneously to avoid delays.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox services are generally not permissible for a WFOE in China. The SAMR and the State Taxation Administration require a physical registered address that is verifiable and where the company's actual business operations are conducted. For a virtual concert and metaverse company, the business may be conducted online, but the registered office must still be a physical location (e.g., a leased office or co-working space) that can receive official correspondence and be subject to inspection. Banks in China typically reject virtual office addresses for corporate account opening, as they require a physical presence for KYC and AML compliance. The local tax bureau may also reject a virtual office for VAT registration and invoice issuance. Therefore, a physical office lease is mandatory, and the lease agreement must be submitted to the SAMR and tax authorities. The office must have a signboard, and the company must maintain a physical presence during business hours.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) SAMR may conduct unannounced inspections to verify the registered address and business operations; (2) Tax authorities may conduct on-site visits to verify the actual business premises and accounting records; (3) Public Security Bureau may inspect for compliance with cybersecurity and data protection laws; (4) The local street office or community committee may conduct periodic checks. Quantified risk: For a virtual concert company with no physical inventory, the risk of inspection is moderate (estimated 30-40% probability within the first year). The risk increases if the company applies for certain licenses or tax incentives. To mitigate, maintain a physical office with a lease agreement, a visible company sign, and a designated person to receive official visits. Ensure that the office is staffed during business hours and that all corporate records are available on-site.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法), Articles 1-8, 128-156, 387-388; Foreign Investment Approval Regulations under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals (外國人投資條例), Articles 7-10
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部), Department of Commercial Affairs (商業司) – Company Registration Section; with prior approval from the Investment Commission (投資審議委員會) for foreign investment
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (公司章程) and Application for Company Registration (公司登記申請書) filed via the Company Registration Online System (公司登記線上申辦系統)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited liability company (有限公司) under Taiwan law; however, the Investment Commission requires a minimum capital of TWD 500,000 (approx. USD 16,000) for foreign-invested service companies, which must be remitted into a Taiwan bank escrow account and certified by a CPA before registration. The capital must remain unencumbered for at least 6 months post-incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (the 'Company'), a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise organized under the laws of Taiwan, Republic of China. This resolution is adopted on [DATE] at [TIME] at the registered office of the Company, with all directors present and constituting a quorum. WHEREAS, the Company has been duly incorporated under the Taiwan Companies Act and has received all necessary approvals from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs; WHEREAS, the shareholders have subscribed to the entire issued share capital of the Company as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board hereby ratifies and confirms the subscription of [NUMBER] shares of common stock, par value TWD [AMOUNT] per share, totaling TWD [TOTAL] (the 'Share Capital'), which has been fully paid in cash into the Company's designated bank account. The Board authorizes the issuance of share certificates to the sole shareholder, [SHAREHOLDER NAME], and directs the corporate secretary to record the same in the share register. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby designates [BANK NAME] and [BANK NAME] as the principal banking institutions of the Company. The Board authorizes the opening of corporate accounts, including a general operating account, a payroll account, and a foreign currency account, and appoints the following individuals as authorized signatories, with any two signatures required for transactions exceeding TWD 500,000: [NAME], [TITLE]; [NAME], [TITLE]; and [NAME], [TITLE]. The Board further authorizes the Chief Financial Officer to execute all banking agreements and to establish online banking protocols in compliance with applicable anti-money laundering regulations. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board adopts the registered office of the Company at [ADDRESS], Taiwan, and authorizes the corporate secretary to file all necessary notices with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and to maintain the statutory records at such address. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board hereby appoints the following officers: [NAME] as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, [NAME] as President and Chief Operating Officer, [NAME] as Chief Financial Officer, and [NAME] as Corporate Secretary. Each officer shall serve at the pleasure of the Board and shall have the authority to execute contracts, open bank accounts, and represent the Company in all ordinary business matters, subject to the limitations set forth in the Company's internal governance policies. 5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes the officers to take all necessary actions, execute all documents, and make all filings required to effectuate the foregoing resolutions, including but not limited to tax registrations, business license applications, and any regulatory permits. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be filed with the corporate records. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned directors have executed this resolution on the date first written above. [SIGNATURE BLOCKS]

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部投資審議委員會) – online portal: https://investtaiwan.org
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Foreign Investment Application Form (外國人投資申請書) along with the investor's certificate of incorporation, audited financial statements (if any), and a detailed business plan describing the virtual concert and metaverse operations. The application must be notarized and apostilled in the investor's home country (China) and translated into Chinese by a certified translator. The Investment Commission reviews the application for compliance with negative lists and national security concerns. Upon approval, a Foreign Investment Approval Letter (核准函) is issued, which is a prerequisite for company registration. Ensure all documents are uploaded in PDF format with a digital signature. The processing time is typically 7-10 business days, but may extend if additional information is requested.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form (Form FIA-1)
Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investor (notarized and apostilled)
Audited financial statements of the investor (last 2 years, if available)
Business plan and projected financials for the Taiwan WFOE
Power of Attorney appointing a local agent (if applicable)
Passport copies of the investor's legal representative
Chinese translation of all foreign-language documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond within 14 days with supplementary documents. If rejected, file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days, or re-submit after addressing the stated deficiencies. Engage a local counsel to expedite the process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Approval and Articles of Incorporation Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs – Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval System (公司名稱及所營事業預查系統)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search to ensure the proposed company name (e.g., 'Taiwan Virtual Concert Metaverse Co., Ltd.') is not identical or confusingly similar to existing entities. File an online application for name pre-approval, specifying the business scope as 'Virtual performance hosting, digital ticketing, and metaverse platform services' (ISIC 7110). Simultaneously, draft the Articles of Incorporation in Chinese, including the company name, business scope, capital structure, and governance rules. The draft must be reviewed by a local attorney to ensure compliance with the Taiwan Companies Act. After name approval (valid for 6 months), proceed to the next step.
required_dossiers: Name Pre-Approval Application Form (online)
Proposed Articles of Incorporation (draft)
Copy of Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Identification documents of the initial directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, modify the name and re-submit. If the Articles are deficient, amend them and re-file. The pre-approval system provides instant feedback; if issues arise, consult the registry's help desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated Bank (e.g., Bank of Taiwan, Cathay United Bank) and a licensed CPA (會計師)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital escrow account in the company's name at a Taiwan bank. Transfer the minimum paid-up capital (TWD 500,000 or higher as per the FIA) from the foreign investor's account. The bank will issue a Capital Deposit Certificate (存款證明). Engage a CPA to verify the capital deposit and issue a Capital Verification Report (資本額查核報告書), which must be submitted with the registration application. The CPA will also confirm that the capital is not from prohibited sources and that the funds are unencumbered. This step must be completed within 15 days of the FIA approval.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Bank account opening documents (company name, passport of representative)
Capital remittance proof (SWIFT or telegraphic transfer)
Capital Deposit Certificate from the bank
CPA engagement letter and verification report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the capital is not received or the CPA raises issues, rectify the remittance or provide additional source-of-funds documentation. If the bank delays, request a written confirmation and escalate to the central bank's foreign exchange department if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration and Business License Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs – Company Registration Online System (公司登記線上申辦系統)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the final Articles of Incorporation, the CPA's Capital Verification Report, the Foreign Investment Approval Letter, the name pre-approval certificate, and the registration application form via the online portal. Pay the registration fee (TWD 3,000, approx. USD 100) and any additional fees for expedited processing. The system will issue a Company Registration Certificate (公司登記證明書) upon approval. After registration, apply for a Business Registration Certificate (營業登記證) from the local tax authority (National Taxation Bureau) to obtain a Uniform Invoice Number (統一編號). This step also triggers the need to register for VAT and other taxes. The entire process typically takes 5-7 business days.
required_dossiers: Completed Company Registration Application Form
Articles of Incorporation (notarized if required)
CPA Capital Verification Report
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Name Pre-Approval Certificate
Identification documents of directors and shareholders
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or title deed)
Power of Attorney for the local agent (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is suspended, the registry will issue a notice of deficiencies. Correct and re-submit within 14 days. If the issue is substantive, such as a conflict with the negative list, appeal to the Investment Commission. In case of rejection, re-apply after rectifying the issues.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – pure digital service provider (ISIC 7110) with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – no industrial operating license required. However, the company must obtain a Business License (營業登記證) and may need a Digital Entertainment Platform License if offering paid virtual events, subject to the Taiwan Digital Entertainment Industry Regulations (數位娛樂產業管理條例).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable – no physical operations, no EIA required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable – zero physical discharge or emissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable – no physical premises beyond a registered office; however, the office must comply with local fire safety regulations (fire extinguishers, evacuation plans) and occupational health and safety standards for office workers, as per the Occupational Safety and Health Act (職業安全衛生法).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), acting through the in-charge local tax service bureaus; electronic filing and registration are performed on the nationwide Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) online portal of the STA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Establish the WFOE with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the enterprise registration process. The issued business license carries the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which operates as the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration identifier under China's multi-license integration reform; no separate TIN or VAT ID application is required after SAMR registration. Within 30 days of business-license issuance, the WFOE must complete post-registration tax information confirmation through the Electronic Tax Bureau, select the in-charge tax bureau, set up fiscal accounting records, register VAT invoice schemes, apply for digital invoice issuance qualification, and, if exporting goods or cross-border services, complete export-tax-filing qualification. A foreign non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment in China is not issued a standalone VAT ID; China-sourced income is subject to withholding by the payer, and the non-resident entity effects registration by filing through the withholding agent or, in the absence of an agent, by making a one-time registration in the Electronic Tax Bureau for the specific income item.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The People's Republic of China does not provide a check-the-box or entity-classification election for a WFOE; the legal entity is by statute a Chinese resident enterprise taxed on worldwide income under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are countered through the general anti-avoidance and Special Tax Adjustment provisions, not through elective tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for basic VAT registration where any taxable business is carried on; mandatory General VAT taxpayer registration applies when annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000. For virtual performance hosting and digital ticketing services the applicable VAT rate is 6%; standard goods sales are 13%/9% as applicable; exports and qualifying cross-border services are zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the Golden Tax system and the fully digitalised electronic invoice (e-invoice) administration regime. All VAT invoices for taxable sales must be issued through the STA-controlled e-invoice platform; issuance data is transmitted in real time to the tax authority. Fully digitalised e-invoices carry a unique 20-digit invoice number, an electronic signature, and a dynamic QR anti-fraud stamp; paper invoices, where still authorised, must be generated through STA-certified tax control equipment. High-volume issuers may use system-to-system interfaces, but every invoice must originate from the official fiscal environment; no third-party private invoice stamping is permitted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from the People's Republic of China may be subject to VAT at 0% when the exporter files a customs export declaration, the goods physically leave China's customs territory, the export sale is supported by a valid overseas contract and invoice, and export proceeds are received from abroad. Cross-border services, including qualifying offshore digital services such as virtual event hosting and metaverse ticketing platforms, are eligible for the 0% rate or VAT exemption when the service is supplied to a recipient located outside China, the service is consumed entirely outside China, and the WFOE retains a copy of the overseas service contract, the bank receipt of offshore payment, and supporting metaverse platform records demonstrating no use of the service in China.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Export) filed through the China International Trade Single Window showing the goods description, quantity, value, destination country and customs clearance status
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of the goods from the Chinese customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent bank foreign-exchange collection voucher matched to the export declaration and SAFE trade-monitoring records
Export VAT invoice issued under the zero-rating code with 0% tax rate and containing the USCC/TIN of the WFOE
Export contract and commercial invoice specifying the overseas buyer and settlement currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unverified or fraudulent export zero-rating claims are subject to recovery of all VAT input credits refunded, collection of the underpaid VAT, and a penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax amount involved under Article 63 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Collection. Cases involving forged customs documents, counterfeit export declarations, or circular repatriation schemes are referred for criminal liability for tax fraud under the Criminal Law; tax authorities may also suspend the WFOE's export-rebate qualification, deny future zero-rated invoices, and conduct retrospective audits of at least the previous five tax years together with related-party foreign-exchange flows.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC), with the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) as co-supervisor for banking and AML licensing; the CBC implements the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, operates interbank NTD clearing, and receives all bank-filed foreign-exchange declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan operates a managed floating exchange-rate regime. The New Taiwan dollar is freely convertible for current-account transactions, including cross-border trade settlements, service fees, wages, and profit remittances, subject to standard reporting through authorized foreign-exchange banks. Capital-account transactions are generally liberalized for direct investment, portfolio investment, and loans, but remain subject to prior approval or declaration to the CBC under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act. A critical nuance for this structure is the mainland-China source of the inbound equity: because the ultimate parent is a people's-republic-of-china enterprise, the inbound remittance will be examined under Taiwan's Regulations Governing Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Chinese Investors and will require the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs to screen the direct investment. Profit remittance is permitted on an arm's-length, tax-cleared basis: dividend distributions to the mainland shareholder require audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, and a CBC-approved foreign-exchange declaration, and are subject to a 10% withholding under the Income Tax Act. Excess volatility is smoothed by the CBC's intervention, which is neither pegged nor a clean float, so treasurers must maintain a disciplined hedging policy. No mandatory conversion ratio exists for export proceeds; enterprises may retain foreign currency in bank accounts, but all receipts must be reported or settled through designated FX banks, and any large-value or suspicious foreign-exchange transaction is reported to the CBC's anti-money-laundering database.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act Article 7 and the CBC Measures Governing Certification of Foreign Exchange Receipts and Disbursements, an exporter of goods is required to receive, settle, or deposit the foreign-currency proceeds with an authorized foreign-exchange bank within 10 calendar days from the date of the export customs declaration; for cross-border services such as virtual-concert ticketing, the trigger date is the service-invoice or contract completion date. There is no mandatory surrender conversion ratio: 100% of export proceeds may be retained in a foreign-currency deposit account or converted into NTD at the exporter's discretion, subject to the CBC large-value foreign-exchange reporting thresholds and a five-year documentary retention rule covering the commercial invoice, bill of lading, service contract, customs entry stamp, and CBC declaration form.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for primary treasury and clearing rails; Medium only as an ancillary collection aggregator. Offshore fintech EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Stripe and similar digital clearing houses) are legally barred from providing Taiwan-domestic deposit-taking, NTD clearing-membership, or local-currency settlement services, because Banking Act Article 29 and the Electronic Payment Institution Act require an FSC license before an intermediary may hold customer funds or clear New Taiwan dollar payments on behalf of a domestic entity. An EMI may enter the flow only as an upstream card-acquiring or payment-aggregation layer processing ticket sales, with all settled receipts swept daily in fiat to a licensed Taiwan Tier-1 bank account. For the USDC leg of this metaverse concert business, the conversion must be executed offshore by a compliant virtual-asset service provider or a fully licensed counterparty before any fiat remittance touches Taiwan; no crypto settlement may occur in the domestic NTD account, and the bank will require written assurance of this separation at onboarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Taiwan's FSC and CBC AML rules mandate that, for a newly incorporated foreign-invested entity, at least one statutory director with account signatory authority and the ultimate beneficial owner(s) must complete an in-branch identity interview at the account-opening branch. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted for a first-time corporate client without an existing banking relationship, although certain banks will accept a notarized power of attorney combined with a live video-call verification for non-resident directors, provided all documents are notarized by a Taiwan notary or certified at a Taipei Economic and Cultural Office post and the bank can independently verify the director's sanctions status. For mainland-China beneficial owners, additional cross-strait document legalization is required, and several domestic banks will decline onboarding unless the mainland controller physically attends or a Taiwan-resident director is mandated. Practical mandate: the statutory director holding a Taiwan ARC or residence status must appear at the branch with the company seal, MOEAIC approval letter, and a complete source-of-funds file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-Strait inbound capital and mainland-China UBO concentration triggering enhanced due diligence and possible sanctioned-crowd or funding-source checks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized or cross-strait-authenticated certificate of incorporation, share register, and articles of association of the mainland parent; three years of Big-4 audited financial statements of the parent; twelve months of parent bank statements from the SAFE-regulated remitting bank; source-of-wealth declarations from each controlling shareholder; the MOEAIC foreign-investment approval letter; and the signed virtual-concert platform contract evidencing the commercial purpose of the capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity and potential nominee-shareholder arrangement: registered WFOE shareholders differ from actual controllers, triggering the Money Laundering Control Act Article 9 reporting duty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Taiwan Company Registrar extract listing all registered shareholders; certified share certificates; board resolution and signed beneficial-ownership undertaking confirming the absence of nominee, trust, or bearer arrangements; identity and residence documents of every individual with at least 10% economic interest; and a completed beneficial-ownership declaration form executed by the statutory director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual-asset and tokenized-ticketing exposure: the concert model uses digital ticket tokenization and USDC receipts, which the bank classifies as VASP/AML high-risk typology covering crypto mixing, unhosted wallets, and unlicensed VASP activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury undertaking that the Taiwan NTD account will never receive or settle USDC; the applicable payment-flow contract with Stripe or a licensed VASP converting crypto to fiat offshore; wallet addresses covered by blockchain-analytics and sanctions-screening reports; an AML policy describing transaction monitoring and suspicious-transaction reporting to the FIU; and an external Taiwan legal opinion confirming that digital ticket tokenization is not a stored-value instrument under the Electronic Payment Institution Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export-proceeds and settlement mismatch: cross-border service receipts from ticket platforms lack physical-performance invoices and transport documents, whereas the CBC export-verification system expects documentary evidence for service exports.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-inbound-remittance e-invoice or payment note complying with Taiwan Uniform Invoice rules; ticket-sales settlement reports from the platform; the ISIC 7110 and NAICS 711310 scope registration certificate; service agreements with artists and venue or rights holders; a tax-clearance certificate proving VAT reporting; and a 12-month export-collections schedule prepared by a Taiwan-certified public accountant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant sequence: (1) obtain Investment Commission (MOEAIC) approval for the mainland-China investor; (2) open at a Tier-1 bank a foreign-investment capital escrow account functioning as the NT dollar injection vehicle; (3) the mainland parent's SAFE-designated bank wires equity through SWIFT MT103 using purpose code 6222 for direct-investment equity, denominated in USD or offshore-converted CNY, with corporate name and investment-approval reference in the remittance narrative; (4) the receiving Taiwan bank converts to NTD, places a freeze pending capital verification, and files the CBC foreign-exchange declaration; (5) a Taiwan CPA performs capital verification and files the capital-verification report with MOEAIC, typically within 15 calendar days; (6) the escrow freeze is released after verification and company registration is updated; (7) any additional shareholder loans are separately declared and must respect Taiwan thin-capitalization and CBC short-term borrowing rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: recurring intercompany royalties, management fees, and concert-licensing fees to the mainland parent via SWIFT MT103 with underlying contracts and CBC declaration, subject to 10% withholding tax or treaty reduction; procurement of audio-visual equipment and virtual-stage software through commercial letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700 by the Taiwan buyer and documentary collections handled as D/P or D/A through the bank's trade-finance desk; all outward payments crossing CBC large-value reporting thresholds require the remitter to present the commercial invoice, contract, and customs or service-completion evidence where applicable; the bank screens counterparties against OFAC, EU, and Taiwan sanctions lists and files the foreign-exchange declaration prior to execution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/TWD forward contracts with a Taiwan authorized FX bank, limited to hedging firm commercial and balance-sheet exposures under the CBC non-speculative requirement
USD/TWD FX swaps matching treasury liquidity maturities
Cross-currency swaps to convert mainland-group CNY exposure into USD/TWD, typically booked offshore with the Taiwan entity's USD-based forward overlay
Plain-vanilla USD/TWD put and call options with premium payments, permitted for hedging ticket-sales receivables
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) trading on USD/TWD is not generally permissible for Taiwan-resident corporates; onshore hedges must be settled deliverable through authorized FX banks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, business report, and profit-distribution proposal approved by shareholders (or by unanimous written shareholder consent for a Taiwan limited company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs, via the Taiwan Company Registration Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end, i.e., on or before June 30 following a December 31 calendar-year close.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance exposes responsible officers to administrative fines of NT$10,000-NT$50,000 under the Taiwan Company Act; the MOEA may order correction, and a company that remains non-operational or fails to remedy repeated violations may be administratively dissolved or struck off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return and undistributed retained-earnings surtax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (R.O.C.), based on the company's tax registration jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 through May 31 of the year following the taxable year; the return must be filed by May 31 for a calendar-year company.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers estimated assessment and penalties under Income Tax Act Articles 108 and 110, generally two times the underpaid tax where a return is filed and up to three times where no return is filed; overdue amounts accrue daily interest at the postal-savings one-year fixed deposit rate and may be referred to administrative enforcement after a 30-day demand period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business tax (value-added tax / gross business receipt tax) bi-monthly return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (R.O.C.)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every bi-monthly period, filed by the 15th day of the following month; e.g., the January-February return is due March 15 and the November-December return is due January 15 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an additional tax of 1% of the tax amount for every two days of delay, capped at 15%; overdue tax also bears statutory interest and is subject to administrative levy if unpaid after 30 days.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner and substantial-controller register annual confirmation / change registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation is finalized as of the shareholders meeting date (by June 30); any qualifying event, including a share transfer causing a shareholder to reach or exceed 10% beneficial ownership or a change in a director or senior manager, must be reported within 15 days of the event. Taiwan does not impose a separate 30-day annual filing window.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update beneficial-owner information within 15 days subjects the responsible person to administrative fines under Company Act Article 22-1, commonly NT$50,000 per occurrence, with repeated non-compliance allowing MOEA correction orders and potential strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company registration renewal / dormant-status declaration (only where status has changed)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) and the municipal commercial registration office where the registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual renewal fee applies to a Taiwan limited company; registration status is evidenced by the May 31 tax return and the June 30 shareholders meeting. Any change to directors, share capital, registered address, or articles must be registered within 15 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unregistered changes carry administrative fines of NT$1,000-NT$5,000 per item; a company that has not commenced business within six months of registration, or has suspended business for more than six months without approved cause, may be administratively dissolved by MOEA under Company Act Article 10.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 20 of the Taiwan Company Act and the MOEA threshold announcement, the operative quantitative audit trigger for this non-public Taiwan limited company is paid-in capital exceeding NT$30 million (approximately USD 937,500 at a 32 TWD/USD reference rate). No separate turnover or headcount audit trigger applies to an ordinary non-public company in the virtual-performance-hosting and digital-ticket industry. If the company becomes a public company or obtains a financial-industry license, it becomes subject to the Financial Supervisory Commission and Securities and Exchange Act audit regime, which mandates independent CPA audits and applies the applicable balance-sheet, turnover, and headcount thresholds for public entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements are prepared under the Taiwan Business Entity Accounting Act and, for this non-public limited company, the Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by the Financial Supervisory Commission; Taiwan-IFRS applies if the company becomes public or enters a regulated financial sector. CPA audit work is performed in accordance with Taiwan Statements on Auditing Standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Taiwan Company Act Article 22-1, a non-public limited company must maintain an accurate substantial-controller / beneficial-owner register at its registered office and report initial beneficial-owner details to the MOEA Company Registration Information System within 15 days of formation. Any subsequent change - including a share transfer that moves a shareholder to or over the 10% threshold or a change in directors or senior managers - must be filed within 15 days of the event. The annual confirmation is completed as part of the shareholders meeting approval process by June 30, at which time the register is certified and the MOEA public record is updated if any change occurred during the year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders Meetings and Board Meetings
Register of Substantial Controllers / Beneficial Owners

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 9,000 per annum if the NT$30 million paid-in-capital audit threshold is exceeded; USD 0 if no statutory audit is triggered.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% (Income Tax Act Article 5, effective for Assessment Year 2018 and thereafter)
